# Implementation Plan: 054 PM4 Per-File Camera Window Cache

**Branch**: `v0.5.0-dev` | **Date**: 2026-06-09 | **Spec**: `wow-viewer/specs/054-pm4-camera-window-cache/spec.md`

**Input**: Feature specification from `wow-viewer/specs/054-pm4-camera-window-cache/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by speckit-plan. The work is library-first and surgical — the spec targets a real UX blocker where every camera jump currently pays a full-decode cost. The fix is per-file caching at two levels (in-memory + on-disk), which lets re-visits and re-shuffles reuse prior work.

## Summary

The current PM4 disk cache keys on the SHA-256 of the camera window's file set, so every camera jump produces a brand-new cache key and pays the full-decode cost again. The fix replaces the per-window blob with a per-file cache: a directory of small entries, one per PM4 file, content-keyed on file stamp. The new cache is hit-or-miss per file, so a camera shift by one tile only pays the cost of the one new tile.

The work lands in three phases (each ≤ 6 steps, each independently validatable). No new external dependencies. The cache version bumps from 7 to 8 (intentional format break; the old per-window cache is invalidated and rebuilt on next use).

## Technical Context

- **Language/Version**: C# 12 / .NET 10 (matches `WowViewer.slnx`)
- **Primary Dependencies**:
  - `wow-viewer/src/viewer/WoWViewer/Terrain/WorldScene.cs` — owns the camera-window load, `_pm4TileObjects`, the `replaceExisting` merge path
  - `wow-viewer/src/viewer/WoWViewer/Terrain/Pm4OverlayCacheService.cs` — owns the on-disk cache blob + `BuildCandidateSignature`
  - `wow-viewer/src/viewer/WoWViewer/Terrain/Pm4OverlayCacheData.cs` (or wherever the cache data records live) — owns the per-tile / per-object record types
  - `wow-viewer/src/viewer/WoWViewer/ViewerApp_Pm4Utilities.cs` — owns the workbench status line display
  - `System.IO.Compression.GZipStream` — keep the existing compression
  - `System.Text.Json` (existing) — for diagnostic export
- **Storage**: New layout `output/cache/pm4-overlay/{dataSourceSegment}/{mapName}/files/{normalizedPath}.pm4cache`. Each file is a small gzip blob.
- **Testing**: `dotnet test wow-viewer/tests/WowViewer.Core.PM4.Tests/WowViewer.Core.PM4.Tests.csproj -c Debug` + a new `WowViewer.Tests` integration test (or `WowViewer.Core.PM4.Tests`) for the cache round-trip.
- **Target Platform**: Windows (`win32`).
- **Project Type**: `library` (new `Pm4PerFileCache` + `Pm4PerFileCacheService`) + `desktop-app` (viewer camera-window load path) + `cli-tool` (none for this spec; inspection lives in the existing tool).
- **Performance Goals**:
  - In-memory re-render: < 100ms per tile (effectively free; O(1) dictionary lookup + GPU buffer reuse).
  - On-disk re-render: < 5s per tile (gzip read + binary deserialization of one file's payload).
  - Fresh-decode path: unchanged from today. No regression.
- **Constraints**:
  - No `H:\CLIENTS` paths. Use staged clients under `I:\parp\parp-tools\output/tmp/wowarchive-clients/`.
  - No writes to `gillijimproject_refactor/`.
  - `AlphaWdtWriter.cs` is frozen (RULE 10) — not touched.
  - Phase 1 visualization is COMPLETE (spec 051 Phase 1) — do not re-implement cube rendering.
  - Cache version bumps 7 → 8 (intentional format break; old on-disk caches invalidate).

**Structure Decision**: New `Caching/` library slice inside the existing `WowViewer.Core.PM4` project. The in-memory cache is a generic data structure usable by any consumer; the on-disk service is a thin file I/O wrapper.

## Implementation Phases

The work is organized into three phases, each at most 6 steps. Each step is independently validatable by `dotnet build` and (where applicable) `dotnet test`.

### Phase 1: Per-File In-Memory Cache (US1, US3) — owner: library + viewer

Steps:
1. **Define `Pm4PerFileCacheEntry`** — `wow-viewer/src/core/WowViewer.Core.PM4/Caching/Pm4PerFileCacheEntry.cs`. Holds the per-tile objects list (re-use `Pm4OverlayCacheTile`-like payload) + position refs + a `LastWriteTicks`/`Length` stamp for content change detection. Pure data record; no I/O.
2. **Define `Pm4PerFileCache`** — `wow-viewer/src/core/WowViewer.Core.PM4/Caching/Pm4PerFileCache.cs`. A `Dictionary<string, Pm4PerFileCacheEntry>` with a configurable LRU cap (default 256). Methods: `TryGet(path, stamp, out entry)`, `Set(path, stamp, entry)`, `Clear()`, `Count`. Pure in-memory; no I/O. Bounded unit tests: insert, hit, stamp mismatch (miss), eviction when cap exceeded.
3. **Wire the in-memory cache into `WorldScene`** — add `private readonly Pm4PerFileCache _pm4PerFileInMemoryCache = new(cap: 256)`. Expose `TryGetPerFileCache(string path, out entry)` and `SetPerFileCache(...)` methods. On `ReloadPm4Overlay()`, also call `_pm4PerFileInMemoryCache.Clear()`. `dotnet build` must pass.
4. **Add a per-file decode path in the camera-window load** — refactor the existing per-tile loop in `LoadPm4OverlayAsync` (around `WorldScene.cs:3670`) so each PM4 file is checked against the in-memory cache before calling `BuildPm4TileObjects`. On hit, the cached entry's objects are added to `_pm4TileObjects` and the file is skipped (no decode, no BuildPm4TileObjects call). On miss, the existing decode path runs, then the result is stored in the in-memory cache. `dotnet build` must pass.
5. **Add per-file progress to `_pm4Status`** — extend the status string in `LoadPm4OverlayAsync` from `PM4 loading: cache miss, decoding {loadCandidates.Count} camera-window files...` to `PM4 loading tile ({tileX},{tileY}) {i}/{total} ({memcacheHits} mem-cache, {diskCacheHits} disk-cache)`. The workbench status line in `ViewerApp_Pm4Utilities.cs:228-235` already reads `_pm4Status`; no UI change needed.
6. **Validate the in-memory cache hit path** — load the staged `development_00_00.pm4`, force a camera window that includes it twice (e.g., load → clear `_pm4TileObjects` only → reload), confirm the second load is a cache hit. Build + run a focused test: `wow-viewer/tests/WowViewer.Core.PM4.Tests/Pm4PerFileCacheTests.cs` covers the in-memory cache behavior. Manual check: status line shows the `mem-cache` count.

Validation gate: `dotnet build` passes. Manual verification shows the in-memory hit for re-visited tiles.

### Phase 2: Per-File On-Disk Cache (US1, US3, US5) — owner: library

Steps:
1. **Define `Pm4PerFileCacheService`** — `wow-viewer/src/core/WowViewer.Core.PM4/Caching/Pm4PerFileCacheService.cs`. Owns the on-disk layout: `output/cache/pm4-overlay/{dataSourceSegment}/{mapName}/files/{normalizedPath}.pm4cache`. Methods: `TryRead(mapName, dataSourceIdentity, path, length, writeTicks, out entry)`, `Write(mapName, dataSourceIdentity, path, entry)`, `Delete(mapName, dataSourceIdentity, path)`. Each entry is a small gzip blob: magic `PM4F`, version `8`, map, path, stamp, payload (per-tile objects + position refs).
2. **Bump the existing on-disk cache version 7 → 8** — `Pm4OverlayCacheService.cs:13`. The old per-window cache blob continues to be readable (it is invalid because of the version mismatch) and the new per-file layout is used instead. The old blob is deleted on the next `TryDelete` cycle or left for the user to clean. `dotnet build` must pass.
3. **Add the per-file read call to the camera-window load** — in the same per-file loop in `LoadPm4OverlayAsync` (the one from Phase 1 Step 4), if the in-memory cache misses, call `Pm4PerFileCacheService.TryRead`. On hit, the payload is materialized into `Pm4OverlayObject` records via the existing `FromCachedLocalized` factory and added to `_pm4TileObjects`. On miss, the existing decode path runs.
4. **Add the per-file write call to the camera-window load** — on a successful fresh decode, call `Pm4PerFileCacheService.Write` with the decoded payload + the file's current `LastWriteTicks`/`Length`. The write is synchronous (small file, fast gzip) and happens before the next file is processed. `dotnet build` must pass.
5. **Add a per-file cache integration test** — `wow-viewer/tests/WowViewer.Core.PM4.Tests/Pm4PerFileCacheTests.cs` gets a new test: `WriteThenRead_RoundTripsPayload` that writes a synthetic `Pm4PerFileCacheEntry` to a temp directory, reads it back, asserts the payload matches. Also `WriteThenRead_StaleStampIsMiss` that writes with stamp A, reads with stamp B, asserts miss. `dotnet test` must pass.
6. **Validate the on-disk cache hit path** — copy `development_00_00.pm4` to a fresh temp `dataSourceIdentity`, run a "first decode + write" pass, then run a "second decode" pass and confirm the second pass reads from disk (no `BuildPm4TileObjects` call). Add the data-source-identity hashing to the cache key path so two different data sources pointing at the same file get different cache entries.

Validation gate: `dotnet build` passes. `dotnet test` shows the per-file round-trip test passing. Manual: a session restart hits the on-disk cache for previously-visited tiles.

### Phase 3: Status, Validation, Memory Bank Sync (US2, US4, FR-004) — owner: viewer + docs

Steps:
1. **Extend the per-file progress format** — the `LoadPm4OverlayAsync` status format from Phase 1 Step 5 gets one more field: `tiles visible=N/M`. The status is updated after each file decode completes. The workbench display in `ViewerApp_Pm4Utilities.cs:228-235` already reads `_pm4Status`; no UI change needed.
2. **Add the "Reload PM4" button behavior** — `ReloadPm4Overlay` (`WorldScene.cs:6174`) now clears the in-memory per-file cache (`_pm4PerFileInMemoryCache.Clear()`) AND invalidates the on-disk per-file cache for the current map. The on-disk entries are deleted (one small file per PM4 file) so the next load forces a fresh decode. The on-disk per-window cache blob (version 7) is also deleted on this path. `dotnet build` must pass.
3. **Add a real-data smoke** — write `wow-viewer/tests/WowViewer.Core.PM4.Tests/Pm4PerFileCacheRealDataTests.cs` that loads the staged `development_00_00.pm4`, decodes it, writes the per-file entry, decodes it a second time via the cache, and asserts the second decode skips `BuildPm4TileObjects`. `dotnet test` must pass.
4. **Update the PM4 canonical doc** — `wow-viewer/docs/architecture/pm4-chunk-semantics.md` gets a one-paragraph "Cache layout" section explaining the per-file directory structure and the new cache version 8.
5. **Update memory bank** — `wow-viewer/memory-bank/activeContext.md` gets a 054 status block (X tasks complete, biggest unproven gap, out-of-scope list). `progress.md` gets a dated entry.
6. **Verify the full UX** — manual end-to-end: load a map, jump far (slow first decode), jump back (fast in-memory hit), close the viewer, reopen, jump to the same area (fast on-disk hit). Document the measured timings in the commit message.

Validation gate: `dotnet build` passes, `dotnet test` shows the new tests passing, manual end-to-end UX matches the spec's success criteria.

## Plan Source of Truth

This file is the single source of truth for the 054 implementation order. When implementation begins, follow phases in order. Each phase ends with the listed validation gate before the next phase starts. If a phase's gate fails, the phase is not done. Fix it. Do not move on.

## Out of Scope (per spec 054)

- Hard memory cap with LRU eviction tuning. The spec includes a simple bounded LRU but does not include eviction policy tuning.
- Networked/shared PM4 cache (per-machine per-session only).
- Predictive pre-fetch.
- Compression changes (we keep gzip for now).
- Migration of the old per-window cache blob to the new per-file format. The old blob is invalidated.
- Any change to the on-disk format of the per-tile object records (lines, triangles, etc.).
